learningObjective: Explain what shape inference computes at the graph-IR level and its limits when dynamic shapes are involved.

canonicalClaims.claim: Graph-level shape inference propagates per-op shape rules from inputs to outputs; when input shapes contain symbolic dims, output shapes are symbolic expressions in those dims. Concretization to integers happens at runtime or via specialization.
conditions: The IR supports symbolic dims / dynamic shape annotations.
The op set provides shape rules per operator.
nonImplications: Does not imply all symbolic outputs collapse to integers before runtime; some remain symbolic.
Does not imply shape inference detects all shape mismatches; op-specific verifiers may still find them.

misconceptions.claim: Shape inference fabricates concrete numbers from observed inputs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It only propagates shape rules; observed inputs are used at runtime, not to invent compile-time constants.
Graph IRs commonly perform static shape inference at compile time.

misconceptions.claim: Any symbolic dim causes the pass to abort and drop shape annotations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Modern IRs handle symbolic dims natively.

misconceptions.claim: Shape inference proves the program semantically correct.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It only propagates shape rules; semantic correctness requires broader analyses.

implementationFacts: ONNX: shape inference over Opset ops
MLIR: shape dialect / op interfaces for shape inference
TVM Relax: symbolic shape propagation via TVMScript / Relax types
performanceScenarios: Downstream fusion and layout passes rely on inferred shapes; better shape info yields tighter kernel selection.
